{{Infobox football league season | competition = Paraguayan Primera División | season = 2003 | dates = 14 February – 26 October 2003 | winners = [[Club Libertad|Libertad]] | promoted = [[Club Nacional (Paraguay)|Nacional]] | relegated = [[Club Sportivo San Lorenzo|San Lorenzo]] | matches = | prevseason = [[2002 Paraguayan Primera División season|2002]] | nextseason = [[2004 Paraguayan Primera División season|2004]] | total_goals = }} The '''2003 Paraguayan Primera División season''' was held from 14 February to 26 October, with the participation of ten clubs. The tournament was divided into three stages: the Torneo Apertura, won by [[Club Libertad|Libertad]]; the Torneo Clausura, also won by Libertad after defeating [[Club Olimpia|Olimpia]] in a penalty shootout tiebreaker. By winning both stages, Libertad was automatically crowned '''Overall Champion of the 2003 season''', securing the tenth league title in its history. == Torneo Apertura 2003 == The Torneo Apertura began on 14 February and concluded on 25 May. === First stage === The first stage was held from 14 February to 20 April. It followed a single round-robin format, with each team playing nine matches. Pld = Matches played; W = Wins; D = Draws; L = Losses; GF = Goals for; GA = Goals against; GD = Goal difference {| style="margin:auto; " |- | style="width: 25px;"| |bgcolor=#ffffff| |- |bgcolor=#ffcc00 style="border: 1px solid black"| |bgcolor=#ffffff |Qualified for [[2004 Copa Libertadores]] |} === Average points === The average points of a team is calculated by dividing its accumulated points over the last three seasons by the number of matches played during that period. === Promotion playoff === This is a two-legged knockout series, with each team playing one match at home, to determine which division each club will play in the following season. It is contested between the second-to-last team in the average points table and the second-placed team from the lower division. The rules stated that if both teams were level on points after the two matches, goal difference would be used to determine the winner. If the tie persisted, a penalty shoot-out would be held. ==== Promotion playoff ==== {{Football box |date = 1 November 2003 |time = 21:15 |team1 = [[Club Atlético 3 de Febrero|3 de Febrero]] |score = 1–2 |report = |team2 = [[Club Tacuary|Tacuary]] |goals1 = Adolfo Fatecha 90+2' |goals2 = Raúl Román 77', 81' |stadium = [[Estadio Antonio Oddone Sarubbi]], [[Asunción]] |attendance = 3,925 |referee = [[Ubaldo Aquino]] (Paraguay)[http://archivo.abc.com.py/2003-11-02/articulos/76776|/tacuary-da-un-paso-importante ABC Digital – Tacuary da un paso importante] }} {{Football box |date = 9 November 2003 |time = 19:05 |team1 = [[Club Tacuary|Tacuary]] |score = 2–1 |report = |team2 = [[Club Atlético 3 de Febrero|3 de Febrero]] |goals1 = Diego Canesa 58'

With an aggregate score of 4–2, Tacuary remained in the Primera División. === Qualification for international tournaments === The accumulated points table was used to determine the APF representatives in CONMEBOL competitions for the following year. * [[2004 Copa Libertadores]] (three qualifiers). The first spot went to the absolute champion of the 2003 Championship ([[Club Libertad|Libertad]]). The second spot went to the Clausura or Apertura champion who was not the absolute champion of 2003 ([[Club Guaraní|Guaraní]], due to a playoff between the two runners-up since Libertad won both tournaments). The third spot was awarded to the winner of the [[2003 Paraguayan Primera División#Pre-Libertadores playoff|Pre-Libertadores playoff]] ([[Club Olimpia|Olimpia]]). === Relegation and promotion playoff === The average points table was used to determine relegation and the playoff participants: * [[Club Sportivo San Lorenzo|San Lorenzo]] was directly relegated to the [[Paraguayan División Intermedia|Second Division]] for finishing last in the average points table.{{Cite web |url=http://archivo.abc.com.py/2003-10-27/articulos/75671/guarani-despide-al-santo-con-un-bendito-empate |title=ABC Digital - Guaraní says goodbye to "Santo" with a blessed draw |access-date=2025-06-27 |archive-date=2016-12-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220085816/http://archivo.abc.com.py/2003-10-27/articulos/75671/guarani-despide-al-santo-con-un-bendito-empate |url-status=dead }} They were replaced by the Intermedia champion, [[Club Nacional (Paraguay)|Club Nacional]]. * [[Club Tacuary|Tacuary]], having the second lowest average, had to play a two-legged promotion playoff against the Intermedia runner-up, [[Club Atlético 3 de Febrero|3 de Febrero]]. The first leg ended with a 2–1 victory for Tacuary. The decisive second leg was also won by Tacuary by 2–1. Ultimately, the team from the higher division secured its spot for one more season with a 4–2 aggregate score. == References == {{reflist}} == External links == * [http://www.rsssf.com/tablesp/para03.html RSSSF - 2003 Season] * [https://web.archive.org/web/20080528085814/http://apf.cerocinco.net/index.php Official website of the Paraguayan Football Association] {{DEFAULTSORT:2003 Paraguayan Primera Division season}} [[Category:Paraguayan Primera División seasons|2003]] [[Category:2003 in South American football leagues]] [[Category:2003 in Paraguayan sport]]
